accuracy.question: Is the diagnosis accurate?
accuracy.answer: Our system provides highly accurate estimates based on real-world car issues and data. While it’s very reliable, we always recommend confirming with a certified professional.

free.question: Is this service free?
free.answer: Yes, the basic diagnosis is completely free. Additional premium features may be added in the future.

time.question: How long does it take?
time.answer: Less than 60 seconds. Just answer a few questions and get your results instantly.

cars.question: What types of cars are supported?
cars.answer: We support most common car brands and models, including petrol, diesel, and hybrid vehicles.

next_steps.question: What should I do after getting the result?

safety.question: Is my data safe?

wrong.question: What if the diagnosis is wrong?

story_modal.title: How Car Safety Was Born
story_modal.intro_1: Car Safety did not begin with code.
story_modal.intro_2: It began with a feeling I saw too often in real life — that moment when a driver knows something is wrong, but has no clear idea what the car is trying to say.
story_modal.quote_4: And before any repair even starts — stress takes over.
story_modal.body_1: As a mechanic, I saw that moment again and again. Not just the fault itself — but the uncertainty around it. People were trying to decide whether to keep driving, whether it was serious, or whether they were about to make it worse.
story_modal.emphasis_title: That moment matters more than most people realise.
story_modal.emphasis_desc: When a car changes, the first thing a driver needs is not noise — they need clarity.
story_modal.body_2: The idea was never to build another generic AI tool. It was to take the way a real mechanic thinks — symptom by symptom, risk by risk, step by step — and turn that into guidance people could access the moment they needed it.
story_modal.pillar_3: Something built around the real questions drivers ask.
story_modal.body_3: Car Safety was shaped from real patterns, repeated problems, and the kind of practical reasoning that only becomes valuable when trust is on the line.
story_modal.closing_1: Because when a car problem begins, trust is not earned by sounding intelligent.
story_modal.closing_2: It is earned by helping someone feel more clear, more grounded, and less alone in the decision they have to make next.
story_modal.closing_final: That is what Car Safety was built to do.
story_modal.cta_footer: Start free · No credit card required

flat_tire.title: Flat Tire Detected
flat_tire.cause: A puncture from road debris or a faulty valve stem.
flat_tire.explanation: Driving on a flat tire will permanently damage your rim and can cause loss of vehicle control.
flat_tire.next_step: Stop immediately in a safe location and change to a spare or call for professional towing.
flat_tire.summary: You have a flat tire. Stop driving immediately to stay safe and protect your rims.

battery.title: Potential Battery Failure
battery.cause: Corroded terminals, battery age, or an alternator issue.
battery.explanation: The engine lacks sufficient power to turn over or may stall unexpectedly.
battery.next_step: Check battery terminals for corrosion and attempt a jump-start using high-quality cables.
battery.summary: Your battery is likely the culprit. Try a jump-start or check the connections.

engine_light.title: Check Engine Indicator
engine_light.cause: Varies from a loose gas cap to a critical sensor malfunction.
engine_light.explanation: The vehicle is likely safe for a short trip to a shop unless the light is flashing.
engine_light.next_step: Ensure your gas cap is tight and get an OBD-II scan at a local garage soon.
engine_light.summary: The check engine light is on. It's usually safe for a short drive, but don't ignore it.

overheating.title: Engine Overheating Alert
overheating.cause: Low coolant, a burst hose, or a failing water pump.
overheating.explanation: Excessive heat will melt engine components, leading to total engine destruction.
overheating.next_step: Pull over and shut off the engine IMMEDIATELY. Do not open the hood if steam is present.
overheating.summary: Your engine is overheating. Pull over and stop immediately to prevent a total rebuild.

leak.title: Fluid Leak Detected
leak.cause: Damaged hose, gasket failure, or cracked reservoir.
leak.explanation: Losing vital fluids like oil or coolant will lead to mechanical failure or overheating.
leak.next_step: Identify the fluid color and check levels. Do not drive if the leak is severe.
leak.summary: You have a visible leak. Check your fluid levels before driving.

smoke.title: Smoke or Burning Smell
smoke.cause: Electrical short, oil leak on hot manifold, or stuck brake caliper.
smoke.explanation: Smoke indicates an active fire risk or severe mechanical friction.
smoke.next_step: Stop immediately and turn off the engine. Evacuate the vehicle if smoke is coming from the cabin.
smoke.summary: Smoke or burning smells are emergency signals. Stop driving immediately.

noise.title: Unusual Mechanical Noise
noise.cause: Worn bearings, loose belts, or failing suspension components.
noise.explanation: Noises are early warning signs of part failure. Ignoring them leads to more expensive repairs.
noise.next_step: Try to identify if the noise changes with speed or engine RPM. Schedule an inspection.
noise.summary: Your car is making an unusual noise. It's best to have it inspected soon.

damage.title: Visible External Damage
damage.explanation: External damage may hide internal structural or mechanical issues.
damage.next_step: Check for fluid leaks and ensure no parts are rubbing against tires.
damage.summary: Visible damage detected. Check for leaks and tire clearance.

unreadable_photo.title: Unreadable Dashboard Photo
unreadable_photo.explanation: We couldn't read this dashboard photo with confidence. The image might be blurry, too dark, or incomplete.
unreadable_photo.next_step: Please upload a clear, close-up photo of your dashboard or describe the warning light in text.

anti_scam.oil_change: Engine flush add-on is rarely needed. Synthetic oil lasts longer — ask if it's included in the quoted price.
anti_scam.tire_rotation: Don't fall for 'nitrogen fill' upcharges — regular air is 78% nitrogen anyway.
anti_scam.brake_inspection: Shops often suggest new rotors with every pad change. Usually, rotors can be resurfaced or left alone if not warped.
anti_scam.air_filter: This is a 2-minute job you can usually do yourself for $15. Shops charge $50+.
anti_scam.battery_check: Most auto parts stores will test your battery for free. Don't pay a shop for just a test.
anti_scam.coolant_check: Coolant flush is only needed every 30k-50k miles. Don't let shops push it at every oil change.

risk_delayed.oil_change: Engine wear, sludge buildup, decreased fuel efficiency, potential engine failure.
risk_delayed.tire_rotation: Uneven tire wear, shortened tire life, decreased traction, potential blowouts.
risk_delayed.brake_inspection: Decreased stopping power, increased braking distance, potential brake failure.
risk_delayed.air_filter: Reduced engine power, poor fuel economy, increased engine wear.
risk_delayed.battery_check: Sudden failure to start, especially in cold weather. Stranding risk.
risk_delayed.coolant_check: Overheating, engine damage, head gasket failure (very expensive).

fluid_guide_tool.title: Fluid Check Guide
fluid_guide_tool.subtitle: General guidance — check owner's manual
fluid_guide_tool.disclaimer: This is a general guide. Locations may vary. Always check when engine is cold unless noted otherwise.

engine_oil.name: Engine Oil
engine_oil.location: Yellow dipstick handle, usually near the front of the engine.
engine_oil.how_to_check: Pull dipstick, wipe clean, reinsert fully, pull again. Oil should be between MIN and MAX marks.
engine_oil.do_not: Never check oil immediately after driving — let the car sit for 5 minutes first.
engine_oil.see_mechanic: If oil is milky, significantly low between changes, or you see metal particles.

coolant.name: Coolant / Antifreeze
coolant.location: Translucent reservoir tank near the radiator, marked with MIN/MAX.
coolant.how_to_check: Check the reservoir level when the engine is COLD. Should be between MIN and MAX.
coolant.do_not: NEVER open the radiator cap when the engine is hot — pressurized steam can cause serious burns.
coolant.see_mechanic: If coolant is disappearing without visible leaks, or if the engine is overheating.

brake_fluid.name: Brake Fluid
brake_fluid.location: Small reservoir on top of the brake master cylinder, near the firewall.
brake_fluid.how_to_check: Check level through the translucent reservoir. Should be between MIN and MAX marks.
brake_fluid.do_not: Don't let brake fluid contact paint — it strips automotive paint. Don't leave the cap off.
brake_fluid.see_mechanic: If fluid is dark, level keeps dropping, or brake pedal feels soft.

power_steering.name: Power Steering Fluid
power_steering.location: Small reservoir with a cap labeled "Power Steering" near the belt area.
power_steering.how_to_check: Some have a dipstick in the cap, others have MIN/MAX marks on the reservoir.
warning_signs: Fluid is dark or has particles
power_steering.do_not: Don't use the wrong type — ATF and power steering fluid are not always interchangeable.
power_steering.see_mechanic: If steering is making noise or if fluid keeps disappearing.

washer_fluid.name: Windshield Washer Fluid
washer_fluid.location: Large reservoir with a windshield/water icon on the cap.
washer_fluid.how_to_check: Open cap and look inside. Refill when low. Use proper washer fluid, not just water.
washer_fluid.do_not: Don't use plain water — it freezes in winter and doesn't clean well. Don't use dish soap.
washer_fluid.see_mechanic: Only if nozzles are broken or the pump motor has failed.

transmission.name: Transmission Fluid
transmission.location: Often near the firewall. Many newer cars are sealed (dealer-only).
transmission.how_to_check: If accessible: engine running, in Park, pull dipstick. Check level and color.
transmission.do_not: Don't overfill — too much fluid causes foaming and erratic shifting.
transmission.see_mechanic: If fluid smells burnt, looks very dark, or you notice any shifting problems.
